description: Original stable_marriage tests.rs and bounded models
state: Two equal-sized populations with complete strict n-entry permutation rows; total 2*n*n entries at most 2000000. Empty populations allowed.
cost: Enumerates sum over n<=3 of (n!)^(2n)=46674 profiles, each with n! assignment candidates and O(n cubed) blocking checks using linear rank lookup. The separate n=1000 accepted boundary uses O(n squared) entries. Fixed bounded exhaustive domain; no scalable testing claim.
forward: Execute original bounded fixtures against independent oracles. Validate equal sizes, checked quadratic budget, then proposer and receiver rows. Build receiver inverse ranks. FIFO free proposers propose to the next untried receiver; a receiver retains its best proposal so far and requeues the rejected proposer. Return receiver index per proposer when the queue empties. Test observations are named pass/fail assertions, not a semantic proof.
inverse: Test observation universe is fixture cases crossed with pass/fail and candidate answers. A pass is excluded if an independently enumerated cover minimum or stable-permutation constraint disagrees, if an expected boundary error differs, or if a repeated witness changes. Universe: two preference matrices crossed with candidate receiver vectors and errors. Absent successful behaviors include a non-permutation, a blocking pair (p,r) where both prefer each other to assigned mates, or a stable permutation giving a proposer a worse partner than another stable permutation. Invalid row lengths/permutations cannot succeed. Unequal sizes beat the budget error, which beats malformed rows; within each row, length beats duplicate/out-of-range entry. The finite exhaustive oracle supports these exact source-derived constraints without a general Rust proof. Untested larger cases are outside the observed test transition universe.

A passing named test has many compatible production programs: arbitrary changes outside the exercised inputs, unused functions or histories can preserve all assertions. A failing optimality assertion retains every candidate answer violating the corresponding enumerated inequality, not a unique bug. For an observed permutation m, retain every pair of complete preference matrices for which m is stable and proposer-optimal: for each stable alternative s and proposer p, rank_p(m[p]) <= rank_p(s[p]). This finite relational characterization is ambiguous: with two proposers each ranking a distinct receiver first, either strict ordering in each receiver row still yields m. Observing a matching loses unproposed suffixes and proposal/rejection history. Error preimages comprise all profiles sharing the first failed validation predicate and observed indices.
limitations: Finite evidence, not proof; allocation failure unmodeled.
Partial syntax, no macro expansion or semantic AST.
